name: Golden Gate Bridge
source: USGS Northern California, West Coast and San Francisco lidar merged (NAVD88 metres). USGS 3DEP public-domain lidar, Entwine Point Tiles: https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/usgs-lidar-public/USGS_LPC_CA_NoCal_Wildfires_B5b_QL1_2018/ept.json and https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/usgs-lidar-public/USGS_LPC_CA_WestCoastElNinoUTM10_2016_LAS_2017/ept.json and https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/usgs-lidar-public/CA_SanFrancisco_1_B23/ept.json
facts: The Golden Gate Bridge is not gold. Its colour is called International Orange, so ships can see it in the fog.
Its two towers rise 746 feet, about 227 metres, above the water, and giant cables hang between them to hold up the road.
axes: +X east, +Y up, +Z south; metres = int16 * scale; y = 0 is the water level
order: random (the first N points are an even subsample)
